title: Clauses to challenge and rapid scripts
content:
Quick brain-dump for 1:1 prep + pocket scripts during redlines. Not polished — meant to be short cues I can read before calls. Keep concise, choose fight vs. trade based on customer size and value.

CONTEXT + GOAL
- Audience: buyer legal / procurement / engineering reviewer.
- Goal: preserve product access and telemetry for inference while minimizing broad IP assignments, limiting liability, and avoiding exfiltration-style data rights.
- Redlines usually cluster around: data use/right to derive, model training/derivative claims, indemnity & cap, security & breach, termination/transition (export), and SLA remedies.

PRINCIPLES (my mental checklist)
- Fight for narrow, purpose-limited data use (processing to provide service, debug, improve).
- Avoid granting rights to use customer data to "train" or create models unless explicit paid program with opt-in.
- Keep liability cap tied to fees (or annual fees) but leave carve-outs for IP indemnity and gross negligence.
- Favor obligations we can operationalize (retention windows, KMS, audit logs) vs open-ended promises ("best efforts" is fine only with metrics).

CLAUSES TO FLAG & QUICK RESPONSES
1) "Customer grants Supplier ... to train and improve models"
   - Flag: blanket training rights.
   - Quick scripts: "We can process data to improve correctness for this customer — for training that updates shared models we need a separate paid program and anonymization guarantees. Can we narrow to 'service improvement and debugging' with opt-out?"
   - Alternate redline language to propose: "Use only to provide the Service to Customer and to improve the Service for Customer's benefit; any use for general model training requires explicit consent and separate compensation."

2) Broad IP assignment on outputs / "work made for hire"
   - Flag: buyer asks for all outputs to be assigned.
   - Script: "For generative outputs we can provide a broad license to use outputs for Customer's internal and product purposes. Assignment of underlying model IP is not possible. Let's propose a perpetual, royalty-free license limited to Customer outputs."

3) Data residency & export commitments
   - Flag: strict residency + export liabilities with heavy indemnities.
   - Script: "We support regionals at Dedicated/Private tiers. For Hosted, we commit to primary processing in X region and provide contractual assurances for transfers with SCCs (or equivalent). For on-prem/VPC we can meet strict residency. Is the ask tied to Hosted?"

4) Indemnity over third-party claims and model outputs (e.g., IP infringement due to generated text)
   - Flag: indemnity unlimited for outputs.
   - Script: "We can indemnify for third-party IP claims that arise from our negligence or breach of representations. We cannot indemnify for Customer's use of outputs or for claims arising from Customer content it supplied. Propose carve-outs: content-supplied-by-Customer; instructions that intentionally infringe; open-ended aggregator claims."

5) Liability caps and consequential damages
   - Flag: no cap or ridiculous cap > revenues.
   - Script: "Standard is cap equal to fees paid in prior 12 months (or 24 months for enterprise). We exclude fraud / willful misconduct / third-party IP indemnity from cap. Would you accept fees-in-12-months?"

6) Audit rights / access to logs / PII requests
   - Flag: customer demands live access/logs or raw transcripts.
   - Script: "We can provide SOC-style reports and audit outputs subject to NDA and a scoped audit process. Live access to raw tenant logs is a Dedicated/Private feature. For Hosted, propose periodic logs + redacted transcripts under a mutual NDA."

7) Subprocessors / subcontractors / cloud providers
   - Flag: blanket approval or customer wants pass-through liabilities.
   - Script: "We maintain a subprocessors list and commit to notify material changes. We remain responsible for subcontractors' compliance. Can we agree on notice + cure process instead of pre-approval for every minor infra change?"

8) Termination for convenience and data return/secure deletion
   - Flag: vague deletion obligations or undefined export formats.
   - Script: "We will export Customer data in common formats within X days and securely delete backups within Y days after all retention windows expire. For Hosted accounts we can retain anonymized telemetry for service improvement unless Customer opts out."

9) SLA metrics & remedies (credits vs. termination)
   - Flag: request for termination based solely on small SLA breaches.
   - Script: "We propose a fixed credit schedule tiered by downtime. Termination right reserved for repeated material breaches after cure period (e.g., 2 incidents within 90 days). Credits are the primary remedy for operational SLO misses."

10) Reverse engineering / model extraction prohibitions
   - Flag: customer forbids any research/commercial use that could be construed as extraction but also claims outputs.
   - Script: "We prohibit deliberate model extraction attempts and will take remediation steps. For outputs, we provide license terms; for research use our Dedicated/Private tiers have restrictions and can be negotiated."

CONCESSION LADDER (order I prefer to yield, cheap --> expensive)
- Admit: non-production telemetry retention for X weeks (cheap).
- Concede: provide SOC2 + penetration test summary (standard).
- Offer: opt-in training program with additional fee (monetize training ask).
- Trade: raise liability cap modestly if they sign on annual committed spend.
- Reject: blanket assignment of our model IP or open-ended training rights.

WALKAWAY / ESCALATION TRIGGERS
- Customer insists on assignment of model IP or rights to use Customer data to train shared models without compensation/notice.
- Unlimited indemnity for all claims including outputs and Customer-supplied content.
- Continuous live access to infra or logs for Hosted tier.
- Excessive redistribution rights for our pre-built models (we must preserve licensing terms for open models and third-party dependencies).

ON-CALL SCRIPTS (30–60s prompts during negotiation)
- When they press on training rights: "We can do a training program but it requires opt-in, anonymization, and a separate fee — otherwise we limit to service improvement and bug fixes. That's consistent with industry practice."
- When they push for deletion + export faster than we can operate: "We can commit to X-day export and deletion timelines; for Hosted there are operational retention windows and backups — we will do a secure purge after those windows expire. If needed, Dedicated gives tighter SLAs."
- When procurement asks for uncapped liability: "We can accept narrow carve-outs outside the cap (fraud, gross negligence), but an uncapped general liability is not something we can agree to; let's propose fees-in-12-months with carve-outs."

SAMPLE CLAUSE LANGUAGE (copy-paste candidates)
- "Customer Data" means data input into the Service by or on behalf of Customer. Supplier may process Customer Data solely to provide the Service and for the purpose of diagnosing and resolving service issues. Any use of Customer Data for general product training or model improvement that benefits other customers shall require Customer's prior written consent and reasonable anonymization.

- "IP Rights": Supplier retains all right, title and interest in the Service, underlying models, and related improvements. Customer is granted a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use outputs generated by the Service for its business purposes.

- "Liability Cap": Except for liability arising from gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraudulent misrepresentation, or Supplier's indemnity obligations for third-party IP claims, Supplier's aggregate liability shall not exceed the fees paid by Customer to Supplier in the 12 months preceding the claim.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODO
- Confirm latest Hosted region guarantees (ask infra: which regions are available and where primary processing occurs).
- Can product produce an export archive with: raw inputs, generated outputs, timestamps, request ids? If not, how close? (Action: ping Rajesh: jira ENG-2018).
- Draft short redline template for 'no-training-without-consent' to use as standard clause.

NOTES TO SELF (call prep)
- Quick framing: "we're here to make your product work reliably; we won't hand over our IP or take uncapped risk; here's where we can flex."
- Keep one example: "If you want training, we can do an optional SLA'd program for x, with anonymization and opt-in. It's chargeable. Otherwise the Service will be improved opportunistically for quality and security, but not used to retrain shared models."
- Bring metrics: typical cap = fees in last 12 months; typical export window = 30 days; SOC2 + pen test summary available on request.

END (save as personal reference; iterate next time after each negotiation call)
